questions.prompt: In the shared responsibility model, which responsibility always remains with the customer regardless of whether the service is IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS?
choices: Operating system patching on all hosts
Data, devices, and accounts and identities
questions.explanation: The customer always owns its data, endpoints, accounts and identities in every cloud model. Physical datacenter, network and hosts are always the cloud provider's responsibility.

questions.prompt: A company moves a line-of-business app from on-premises VMs to Azure virtual machines (IaaS). Who is responsible for patching the guest operating system?
choices: Shared equally by Microsoft and the customer
questions.explanation: With IaaS the customer manages the operating system, including updates and patches. Microsoft manages the physical host, network and datacenter.

questions.prompt: Which cloud service model places the MOST responsibility on the cloud provider?
questions.explanation: In SaaS the provider manages the application, runtime, OS and infrastructure, leaving the customer mainly responsible for data, identities and devices.

questions.prompt: In an on-premises datacenter, who is responsible for the physical security of the servers?
choices: The organization that owns the datacenter
Responsibility is shared with the cloud provider
questions.explanation: On-premises, the organization owns every layer of the stack, including physical security. Shared responsibility only shifts duties once workloads move to the cloud.

questions.prompt: Which statement BEST describes the defense-in-depth strategy?
choices: Placing all security controls at the network perimeter firewall
Encrypting all data in the organization with a single master key
Granting users full access and auditing their actions afterwards
Layering several security controls so one failure doesn't expose the asset
questions.explanation: Defense in depth uses layered controls (physical, identity, perimeter, network, compute, application, data) so that no single failure exposes the data.

questions.prompt: In the defense-in-depth model, which layer is at the center and is the ultimate target being protected?
questions.explanation: Data sits at the center of the layered model; attackers ultimately want to access or exfiltrate data, so every outer layer exists to protect it.

questions.prompt: A security team deploys DDoS protection on its internet-facing endpoints. Which defense-in-depth layer does this control MOST directly address?
questions.explanation: The perimeter layer protects against network-based attacks from the internet, such as distributed denial-of-service floods.

questions.prompt: Which defense-in-depth layer is addressed by limiting communication between resources through segmentation and deny-by-default rules?
questions.explanation: The network layer focuses on segmentation and restricting traffic between resources so attackers cannot move laterally.

questions.prompt: Keeping virtual machines patched and closing unneeded ports on them is part of which defense-in-depth layer?
questions.explanation: The compute layer secures access to virtual machines and keeps them patched and hardened.

questions.prompt: What are the three components of the CIA triad?
questions.explanation: The CIA triad describes the core security goals: keep data confidential, keep it accurate and unaltered, and keep it available to authorized users.

questions.prompt: An attacker alters the amounts in a payroll file without being detected. Which CIA triad principle has been violated?
questions.explanation: Integrity means data remains accurate and unaltered by unauthorized parties. Confidentiality would be violated if the data were only read.

questions.prompt: A ransomware attack encrypts a hospital's patient records so staff cannot open them. Which CIA principle is MOST directly affected?
questions.explanation: Availability means authorized users can access data when needed; ransomware that locks files primarily denies that access.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is one of the three guiding principles of the Zero Trust model?
questions.explanation: The Zero Trust principles are verify explicitly, use least privileged access, and assume breach. Zero Trust explicitly rejects trusting the corporate network by default.

questions.prompt: Under the Zero Trust principle 'verify explicitly', what should an organization do?
choices: Base each access decision on all available signals
Verify users only during their first sign-in of each working day
Trust any request that originates from inside the corporate network
Rely solely on perimeter network firewalls to validate access requests
questions.explanation: Verify explicitly means every access decision uses all available signals, not just network location.

questions.prompt: Granting users just-in-time and just-enough access with risk-based adaptive policies BEST illustrates which Zero Trust principle?
questions.explanation: Least privileged access limits users with JIT/JEA, risk-based adaptive policies and data protection.

questions.prompt: A company segments access, uses end-to-end encryption, and uses analytics to detect threats on the expectation that attackers may already be inside. Which Zero Trust principle is this?
questions.explanation: Assume breach means minimizing blast radius through segmentation, encryption and continuous threat detection.

questions.prompt: Which item is one of the six foundational pillars that Zero Trust policies are applied to?
questions.explanation: Microsoft lists six Zero Trust pillars: identities, devices, applications, data, infrastructure, and networks.

questions.prompt: What is the PRIMARY difference between symmetric and asymmetric encryption?
choices: Symmetric encryption cannot be decrypted, but asymmetric encryption can
Symmetric uses one shared key; asymmetric uses a public/private key pair
Symmetric uses a key pair; asymmetric uses a single shared secret key
Symmetric is used only for data at rest; asymmetric only for data in transit
questions.explanation: Symmetric encryption shares one secret key, while asymmetric encryption uses a mathematically related public/private key pair.

questions.prompt: Which type of encryption protects data stored on a physical disk, such as a database file on a server?
questions.explanation: Encryption at rest protects stored data so it cannot be read without the keys even if the storage is stolen.

questions.prompt: A web application uses TLS when users submit forms. What type of protection does this provide?
questions.explanation: TLS encrypts data as it moves across the network, which is encryption in transit.

questions.prompt: Which statement about hashing is correct?
choices: Hashing produces different output each time for the same input
Hashing produces a fixed-length value and is not designed to be reversed
Hashing is mainly used to compress large files
Hashing uses a private key to restore the original text
questions.explanation: A hash function is deterministic and one-way, producing the same fixed-length output for the same input; it is not decrypted back to the original.

questions.prompt: Why do systems typically store hashed passwords rather than encrypted passwords?
choices: Hashing requires no computation at all when a user signs in
Hashes are one-way, so the password can't be recovered from them
Hashes are shorter, which greatly reduces the database storage needed
Encrypted passwords cannot be compared with user input during sign-in
questions.explanation: Storing a one-way hash lets the system verify a password by hashing the input and comparing, without ever keeping a recoverable copy.

questions.prompt: A developer notices two users with the same password have different stored hashes. What is the MOST likely reason, known as salting?
choices: Truncating each hash to a shorter length to save storage
Encrypting the stored hash with the user's public key
Adding random data to a password before it is hashed
Storing copies of each hash in two separate databases
questions.explanation: A salt is random data added before hashing, which defeats precomputed rainbow-table attacks and hides identical passwords.

questions.prompt: Which concept refers to protecting data that is being actively processed in memory, for example in a trusted execution environment?
questions.explanation: Encryption in use (confidential computing) protects data while it is processed, typically inside a hardware-based trusted execution environment.

questions.prompt: In governance, risk, and compliance (GRC), what does 'governance' refer to?
choices: Encrypting sensitive data according to the requirements of regulatory standards
The rules, practices, and processes used to direct and control an organization
Adherence to laws and regulations that are set by external authorities
The process of identifying and assessing potential threats to the organization
questions.explanation: Governance is how the organization directs and controls itself through rules and processes; risk management and compliance are the other two GRC components.

questions.prompt: A compliance officer must ensure the company follows regulations issued by an external authority. Which GRC component does this BEST describe?
questions.explanation: Compliance is adhering to laws, regulations, standards and policies defined by external bodies or the organization.

questions.prompt: Which GRC component involves identifying, assessing, and responding to threats that could affect an organization's objectives?
questions.explanation: Risk management identifies and evaluates threats and decides how to respond, such as accepting, mitigating or transferring the risk.

questions.prompt: What does the compliance term 'data residency' refer to?
choices: The concept that data is subject to the laws of the country where it is held
The minimum length of time data must be retained before it can be deleted
The person or team within the organization who owns a particular dataset
Rules on where data is physically stored and how it moves between regions
questions.explanation: Data residency concerns where data is physically stored and moved. Data sovereignty is the related idea that data is subject to local laws.

questions.prompt: A multinational stores customer data in Germany and must follow German law for that data. Which concept does this describe?
questions.explanation: Data sovereignty means data is subject to the laws and regulations of the country or region where it is collected, held or processed.

questions.prompt: Which compliance concept focuses on giving people transparency and control over how their personal data is collected and used?
questions.explanation: Data privacy is about notifying people and giving them control over the collection, use and processing of their personal data.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
choices: They are two names for the same process
Authentication grants permissions; authorization verifies identity
Authentication proves who you are; authorization determines what you are allowed to do
Authentication applies only to devices; authorization applies only to users
questions.explanation: Authentication (AuthN) verifies identity, while authorization (AuthZ) decides the level of access a verified identity receives.

questions.prompt: A user signs in successfully but receives an 'access denied' message when opening the finance share. Which process denied the access?
questions.explanation: The user was already authenticated; the decision about what resources they can access is authorization.

questions.prompt: Why is identity often described as the new primary security perimeter?
choices: Identities cannot be compromised in the way networks can be breached
Users work from many devices and locations outside the network boundary
Regulations now prohibit organizations from using network-based controls
Cloud providers no longer support network firewalls for their services
questions.explanation: With cloud services, mobile devices and remote work, the network edge has dissolved, so identity controls are central to securing access.

questions.prompt: Which of the four pillars of an identity infrastructure is concerned with tracking who does what, when, where, and how?
questions.explanation: The four identity pillars are administration, authentication, authorization and auditing; auditing records activity to detect issues and support compliance.

questions.prompt: Which identity pillar covers the creation and management of identities for users, devices, and services?
questions.explanation: Administration is about creating, governing and managing identities and their lifecycle.

questions.prompt: In modern authentication, what is the role of an identity provider (IdP)?
choices: It stores application data on behalf of signed-in users
It authenticates users and issues trusted security tokens
It encrypts network traffic flowing between datacenters
It hosts the business applications that users sign in to
questions.explanation: A central identity provider such as Microsoft Entra ID verifies identities and issues tokens, so individual apps do not need to manage credentials.

questions.prompt: A user signs in once and can then access several applications without being prompted again. What capability is this?
questions.explanation: SSO lets a user authenticate once with an identity provider and access multiple trusted applications without re-entering credentials.

questions.prompt: A company wants partner users to access its apps using sign-ins performed by the partner's own identity provider. What identity concept is this?
choices: Encrypting identity data at rest using a customer-managed key
Copying all user accounts into every application's local user database
A trust that lets one domain accept another identity provider's authentication
Merging two separate directories into a single Microsoft Entra tenant
questions.explanation: Federation establishes trust between domains so one domain accepts authentication performed by another identity provider.

questions.prompt: In a federation trust, does trust always flow in both directions?
choices: No, federation trust is not necessarily bidirectional
Yes, but only between Microsoft services
Yes, federation always creates a two-way trust
questions.explanation: A federation trust can be one-way: domain A may trust domain B without B trusting A.

questions.prompt: Which on-premises service is Microsoft's traditional directory service for Windows Server domains?
questions.explanation: AD DS is the traditional on-premises directory service; Microsoft Entra ID is the cloud-based identity and access management service.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of a directory service?
choices: To store and organize information about objects such as users, groups, and devices
To route network traffic between subnets and remote sites
To encrypt files stored on endpoint devices and removable drives
To host web applications and their back-end databases
questions.explanation: A directory service is a hierarchical store of objects and their attributes that supports authentication and management.

questions.prompt: Which threat involves an attacker trying a few commonly used passwords against many accounts to avoid lockouts?
choices: Brute force against a single account
questions.explanation: Password spray tries a small number of common passwords across many accounts, staying under per-account lockout thresholds.

questions.prompt: An attacker emails users a fake sign-in page that looks like the corporate portal to collect credentials. What type of attack is this?
questions.explanation: Phishing tricks users into revealing credentials or other sensitive information through deceptive messages and sites.

questions.prompt: A targeted phishing email is crafted for a specific employee using details from their social media profile. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Spear phishing is phishing aimed at a specific person or group using tailored information to appear legitimate.

questions.prompt: An admin reviews a service account that has Owner rights on every subscription but only reads one storage account. Which principle is being violated, and what does it state?
choices: Administrators keep permanent full access to all systems
Users share accounts to reduce administrative overhead
Permissions are granted broadly and revoked after an incident
Users and services get only the minimum permissions they need
questions.explanation: Least privilege reduces risk by limiting access to what is strictly required for a role or task.

questions.prompt: Which statement BEST describes the relationship between Microsoft Entra ID and AD DS?
choices: Microsoft Entra ID is simply AD DS running on Azure virtual machines
AD DS must be deployed before any Microsoft Entra ID tenant can exist
They use identical protocols, such as Kerberos and NTLM, for all apps
Microsoft Entra ID is a cloud identity service, not a cloud copy of AD DS
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID is designed for cloud apps and uses modern protocols like OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect and SAML; it does not natively provide Kerberos-based domain features or Group Policy like AD DS.

questions.prompt: Which feature of AD DS is NOT natively provided by Microsoft Entra ID?
questions.explanation: Group Policy is an AD DS feature; Microsoft Entra ID offers SSO, MFA and Conditional Access instead.

questions.prompt: A security team wants to reduce the attack surface by disabling unused services and closing unnecessary ports. What security concept is this?
questions.explanation: Hardening reduces the attack surface by removing unnecessary software, services, ports and default settings.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an example of a digital certificate's purpose?
choices: Compressing data before it is transmitted
Storing a user's password in plaintext form
Binding a public key to a verified identity
Assigning IP addresses to network devices
questions.explanation: A digital certificate, issued by a certificate authority, binds a public key to a subject so parties can trust that key.

questions.prompt: A US healthcare provider must protect patient data as required by HIPAA. Meeting this legal obligation is an example of what?
questions.explanation: Following laws like HIPAA is regulatory compliance, a core part of GRC.

questions.prompt: What is an 'attack chain' (kill chain) in security concepts?
choices: A backup rotation schedule for protecting critical data
The sequence of stages an attacker follows to reach an objective
A set of firewall rules processed in priority order
A list of approved security vendors and their products
questions.explanation: Modeling attacks as a chain of stages helps defenders detect and break the attack at multiple points.

questions.prompt: Which type of malware encrypts a victim's files and demands payment to restore access?
questions.explanation: Ransomware denies access to data, often by encrypting it, and demands a ransom for the decryption key.

questions.prompt: A company relies only on a firewall at its network edge and trusts all internal traffic. Which approach does this represent, in contrast to Zero Trust?
choices: The Zero Trust principle of assume breach
The Zero Trust principle of verify explicitly
The Zero Trust principle of least privileged access
questions.explanation: Trusting everything inside the network is the classic perimeter model that Zero Trust replaces with continuous verification.

questions.prompt: Which type of identity should be used for an application or service, rather than a person, to access resources?
questions.explanation: Workload identities (applications, service principals, managed identities) let software authenticate without using a human user's credentials.

questions.prompt: A user who left the company still has an active account, which is later misused. Which identity pillar MOST directly failed?
questions.explanation: Administration covers the identity lifecycle, including removing access when people leave; failing to deprovision is an administration gap.

questions.prompt: What is Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: A cloud identity and access management service
An on-premises domain controller server role
A cloud data loss prevention service for email
An endpoint antivirus and anti-malware product
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory) is Microsoft's cloud identity and access management service.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra ID object represents an application's identity in a specific tenant and is used to assign it permissions?
questions.explanation: A service principal is the local representation of an application in a tenant, defining what the app can access.

questions.prompt: A developer needs an Azure VM to access Azure Key Vault without storing any credentials in code. What should they use?
questions.explanation: Managed identities are automatically managed by Azure, so applications can authenticate to services without developers handling secrets.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a system-assigned and a user-assigned managed identity?
choices: System-assigned can be assigned to many resources; user-assigned can be assigned to only one
Only user-assigned identities are able to authenticate to Microsoft Entra ID
System-assigned is tied to one resource's lifecycle; user-assigned is standalone and shareable
System-assigned identities require a client secret that developers store in their code
questions.explanation: Deleting the resource deletes its system-assigned identity, while a user-assigned identity is created separately and can be attached to multiple resources.

questions.prompt: Which type of identity in Microsoft Entra ID represents a physical device such as a laptop or phone?
questions.explanation: Device identities let Microsoft Entra ID know about devices so administrators can apply policies such as requiring compliant devices.

questions.prompt: A company's laptops are joined to on-premises AD DS and also registered in Microsoft Entra ID. Which device state is this?
questions.explanation: Hybrid joined devices are joined to on-premises AD DS and registered with Microsoft Entra ID.

questions.prompt: Employees use personal phones (BYOD) to access corporate email, signing in with their work account. Which device identity option fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra registered is designed for personally owned devices, signed in with a personal account and a work identity added.

questions.prompt: A cloud-first organization wants new Windows laptops joined directly to Microsoft Entra ID with no on-premises domain. Which option should it use?
choices: Workplace Join via AD FS only
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra joined devices are organization-owned and signed in with an organizational Microsoft Entra account, with no AD DS required.

questions.prompt: Which group type in Microsoft Entra ID is used to grant access to shared resources and can contain users, devices, and service principals?
questions.explanation: Security groups manage access to resources. Microsoft 365 groups are for collaboration and contain only users.

questions.prompt: A team lead wants a group that automatically gets a shared mailbox and SharePoint site. What is a key characteristic of a Microsoft 365 group compared with a security group?
choices: It can contain devices and service principals as members
It cannot be used as the basis for a Microsoft Teams team
It provides a shared mailbox, calendar, and SharePoint site
It is available only in on-premises Active Directory DS
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 groups give members shared collaboration resources, and their membership is limited to users.

questions.prompt: An admin wants users to be added to a group automatically when their department attribute equals 'Sales'. What should the admin use?
questions.explanation: Dynamic membership rules add or remove members automatically based on user or device attributes.

questions.prompt: Which tool synchronizes identities from on-premises AD DS to Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: Microsoft Entra Connect or Cloud Sync
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and Cloud Sync provision hybrid identities from AD DS into Microsoft Entra ID.

questions.prompt: With which hybrid authentication method is a hash of the on-premises password hash synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID so it can authenticate users in the cloud?
questions.explanation: Password hash synchronization syncs a hash of the password hash, letting Microsoft Entra ID validate sign-ins directly in the cloud.

questions.prompt: An organization requires that passwords are validated only against on-premises domain controllers, but does not want to deploy AD FS. Which method should it choose?
questions.explanation: Pass-through authentication uses lightweight on-premises agents to validate passwords against AD DS without a federation infrastructure.

questions.prompt: Which hybrid authentication method hands off authentication to a separate trusted system such as AD FS?
questions.explanation: With federation, Microsoft Entra ID redirects sign-ins to a trusted identity provider like AD FS, which performs the authentication.

questions.prompt: What is a key benefit of password hash synchronization compared with pass-through authentication?
choices: Password hashes never leave the on-premises network
Cloud sign-in still works if on-premises servers are down
It enforces on-premises sign-in hour restrictions in real time
It requires deploying and maintaining AD FS servers
questions.explanation: Because the password hash is in the cloud, sign-in does not depend on on-premises agents; PHS also enables leaked credential detection.

questions.prompt: A consultant from another company is invited to a project and appears in the tenant as a guest. What is a guest user in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: An external user invited to collaborate in the tenant
A temporary employee account that has no password set
An administrator who has only read-only directory access
A service account that runs scheduled background jobs
questions.explanation: Guests are external identities, typically invited through B2B collaboration, who get limited access to the tenant's resources.

questions.prompt: A company wants to share a Teams channel and SharePoint documents with a partner's employees, letting them sign in with their own work accounts. Which capability should it use?
questions.explanation: B2B collaboration invites external users as guests who authenticate with their own credentials, so the company doesn't manage their passwords.

questions.prompt: A retailer is building a customer-facing shopping app and wants customers to sign up with email or social accounts. Which Microsoft Entra capability is designed for this?
choices: Microsoft Entra External ID for customer (external tenant) scenarios
Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration in the workforce tenant
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra External ID in an external tenant handles customer identity and access management, including self-service sign-up and social sign-in.

questions.prompt: What does B2B direct connect enable?
choices: A mutual trust with another Microsoft Entra organization without guest accounts
Synchronizing on-premises AD DS users to the Microsoft Entra ID tenant
Federating with Google consumer accounts for customer-facing apps
Creating local accounts for partner employees in on-premises AD DS
questions.explanation: B2B direct connect lets users from a trusted partner organization access resources like Teams shared channels without being added as guests.

questions.prompt: Which settings let an admin control which external organizations users can collaborate with and whether inbound or outbound B2B access is allowed?
questions.explanation: Cross-tenant access settings control inbound and outbound B2B collaboration and direct connect with specific external Microsoft Entra organizations.

questions.prompt: Which authentication method category is considered the MOST secure and least vulnerable to phishing?
choices: One-time codes sent by SMS text message
Passwordless methods such as FIDO2 keys
Verification codes read out by voice call
questions.explanation: FIDO2 security keys and other passwordless methods are phishing-resistant, whereas passwords and SMS can be phished or intercepted.

questions.prompt: What does multifactor authentication (MFA) require?
choices: A password that is changed every 30 days
Two passwords entered one after the other
Signing in from two different devices at once
Two or more different types of verification factors
questions.explanation: MFA combines different factor categories: knowledge, possession, and inherence. Two passwords are the same factor.

questions.prompt: A user signs in with a password and then approves a notification in Microsoft Authenticator. Which factor does the app approval represent?
questions.explanation: The approval proves possession of the registered phone, which is a possession factor.

questions.prompt: Using a fingerprint to unlock Windows Hello for Business represents which authentication factor?
questions.explanation: Biometrics such as fingerprints or facial recognition are inherence factors.

questions.prompt: Which free feature provides a baseline level of protection, including requiring MFA registration and blocking legacy authentication, for tenants that don't use Conditional Access?
questions.explanation: Security defaults are preconfigured settings that enforce MFA registration, require MFA when needed and block legacy authentication protocols.

questions.prompt: An organization has Microsoft Entra ID P1 and wants custom rules for when MFA is required. What should it use instead of security defaults?
questions.explanation: Conditional Access provides granular, customizable control over MFA and other access requirements; security defaults are a fixed baseline.

questions.prompt: Why does blocking legacy authentication improve security?
choices: Legacy protocols can't enforce MFA, so attackers use them for password attacks
Legacy authentication stores user passwords in plaintext in Microsoft Entra ID
Legacy authentication protocols are required for passwordless sign-in methods
Legacy protocols are much slower than modern authentication protocols
questions.explanation: Older protocols such as POP, IMAP and SMTP basic auth cannot perform MFA, so attackers use them for password spray attacks.

questions.prompt: Which passwordless option uses a PIN or biometric tied to a specific Windows device?
questions.explanation: Windows Hello for Business replaces passwords with strong two-factor authentication bound to the device, unlocked by a PIN or biometric.

questions.prompt: A user signs in without a password by entering a number shown on screen into the Microsoft Authenticator app. Which method is this?
choices: A Temporary Access Pass issued by an admin
An OATH software token in a third-party app
Windows Hello for Business on a laptop
questions.explanation: Authenticator phone sign-in lets the user approve with number matching and a biometric or PIN on the phone instead of a password.

questions.prompt: A security team is evaluating hardware tokens for administrators. What is a FIDO2 security key?
choices: A one-time code delivered to the user's phone by text message
A long random password stored in a password manager vault
A certificate stored in Azure Key Vault for application access
A hardware key used for phishing-resistant passwordless sign-in
questions.explanation: FIDO2 keys use public key cryptography bound to the site's origin, providing passwordless and phishing-resistant sign-in.

questions.prompt: What are passkeys in Microsoft Entra ID based on?
choices: FIDO2 standards using public/private key pairs
Shared secrets synced by SMS messages
questions.explanation: Passkeys are FIDO2 credentials based on public/private key pairs; Microsoft Entra ID supports passkeys in Microsoft Authenticator and on FIDO2 security keys, and they are phishing-resistant.

questions.prompt: Which authentication method uses X.509 certificates for sign-in to Microsoft Entra ID without requiring federation with AD FS?
choices: Email one-time passcode for guest users
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra CBA lets users authenticate directly with X.509 certificates, such as on smart cards, and is phishing-resistant.

questions.prompt: An admin needs to give a new employee a time-limited code so they can sign in and register passwordless credentials on their first day. What should the admin issue?
choices: A FIDO2 key belonging to another user
questions.explanation: A Temporary Access Pass is a time-limited passcode that lets users onboard or recover and register strong authentication methods.

questions.prompt: Which authentication method is generally considered the LEAST secure secondary method because messages can be intercepted or SIM-swapped?
questions.explanation: SMS remains supported but is weaker due to SIM-swapping and interception risks; phishing-resistant methods are preferred.

questions.prompt: Which feature lets users reset their own forgotten password without contacting the help desk?
questions.explanation: SSPR lets users reset or unlock their accounts after verifying their identity with registered methods.

questions.prompt: For SSPR in a hybrid environment, which feature writes password changes made in the cloud back to on-premises AD DS?
questions.explanation: Password writeback, configured through Microsoft Entra Connect or Cloud Sync, writes cloud password resets back to on-premises AD DS.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra feature blocks users from setting weak passwords such as known breached terms or company-specific words?
questions.explanation: Password Protection uses a global banned password list and an optional custom list to reject weak passwords, including on-premises with agents.

questions.prompt: A company wants to stop users from choosing passwords containing its product names. What should it configure?
questions.explanation: The custom banned password list adds organization-specific terms to the global banned list.

questions.prompt: Attackers are repeatedly guessing passwords for a user who is also trying to sign in normally. What is Microsoft Entra smart lockout designed to do?
choices: Permanently disable accounts after one failed sign-in
Lock any device that is not marked as compliant
Lock out attackers while letting legitimate users sign in
Force users to change their password every week
questions.explanation: Smart lockout distinguishes sign-ins from familiar locations and locks out attackers after repeated failures.

questions.prompt: What do Conditional Access policies fundamentally consist of?
choices: Password complexity and expiration rules for all users
If-then statements combining signals with access decisions
A single list of IP addresses that are allowed to sign in
Role assignments that give administrators directory permissions
questions.explanation: Conditional Access evaluates signals such as user, location, device and risk, then applies decisions like block, grant, or require MFA.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a signal that Conditional Access can evaluate?
choices: The location from which the user is signing in
The amount of free disk space on the server
The size of the user's mailbox
The user's job title on their business card
questions.explanation: Signals include user or group membership, IP location, device, application, and real-time and calculated risk.

questions.prompt: A company wants to require MFA only when users access the HR app from outside the corporate network. Which feature BEST meets this need?
questions.explanation: Conditional Access can target a specific cloud app and use named locations to require MFA only from untrusted networks.

questions.prompt: Which Conditional Access decision completely prevents access?
questions.explanation: Block access is the most restrictive decision; grant decisions allow access, optionally after satisfying controls.

questions.prompt: Which Conditional Access grant control requires that a device meets Microsoft Intune compliance requirements?
choices: Require device to be marked as compliant
questions.explanation: Conditional Access can require a device marked compliant by Intune before granting access.

questions.prompt: A security team wants to see what impact a new Conditional Access policy would have before enforcing it. What should they do?
questions.explanation: Report-only mode evaluates and logs the policy's result without enforcing it, so admins can assess impact.

questions.prompt: When are Conditional Access policies enforced?
choices: Before the user has entered a username
Only when the user's password has expired
Only once per month for each registered user
questions.explanation: Conditional Access is evaluated after first-factor authentication; it is not a frontline defense against scenarios like denial-of-service attacks.

questions.prompt: A bank wants users of its trading app to reauthenticate every four hours. What does the Conditional Access session control 'sign-in frequency' define?
choices: How many devices a user is allowed to register
How often access reviews run for privileged roles
The maximum number of characters in a password
How long before users must sign in again to a resource
questions.explanation: Sign-in frequency sets the time period before a user is prompted to sign in again when accessing a resource.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra ID license is required to use Conditional Access?
choices: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher
No license is required at all
questions.explanation: Conditional Access requires Microsoft Entra ID P1, which is included in P2 and many Microsoft 365 plans.

questions.prompt: A company wants risk-based Conditional Access that requires MFA when a sign-in is flagged as medium risk. Which license is needed?
questions.explanation: Sign-in risk and user risk conditions come from Microsoft Entra ID Protection, which requires Microsoft Entra ID P2.

questions.prompt: A CISO wants automated detection of compromised accounts. What is the purpose of Microsoft Entra ID Protection?
choices: To manage just-in-time activation of administrator roles
To scan email attachments for malware before delivery
To classify documents and email with sensitivity labels
To detect and remediate identity risks such as leaked credentials
questions.explanation: ID Protection uses signals and machine learning to detect identity risks and can feed risk into Conditional Access.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between sign-in risk and user risk in Microsoft Entra ID Protection?
choices: User risk is calculated on-premises; sign-in risk is calculated in the cloud
They are identical measures that are reported under different names
Sign-in risk rates a single authentication; user risk rates the whole identity
Sign-in risk applies only to devices; user risk applies only to apps
questions.explanation: Sign-in risk is evaluated per authentication attempt, while user risk reflects the likelihood that the account has been compromised.

questions.prompt: A user's credentials appear in a public dump on the dark web. Which ID Protection risk detection is triggered?
questions.explanation: Leaked credentials is a user risk detection raised when a user's valid credentials are found in leaks.

questions.prompt: A user signs in from New York and, 30 minutes later, from Sydney. Which ID Protection risk detection is MOST likely triggered?
questions.explanation: Atypical travel flags sign-ins from geographically distant locations within a time too short to physically travel.

questions.prompt: A sign-in comes from a Tor browser exit node. Which risk detection does this MOST likely generate?
questions.explanation: Anonymous IP address detections indicate sign-ins from anonymizing proxies such as Tor or anonymous VPNs.

questions.prompt: A user risk policy is configured so high-risk users must remediate. What is a typical remediation required by such a policy?
choices: Removing the user from all groups
questions.explanation: User risk policies commonly require a secure password change (after MFA) so users can self-remediate.

questions.prompt: Which ID Protection report shows users flagged as potentially compromised, along with their risk level?
questions.explanation: The risky users report lists users at risk, the detections involved and the history, so admins can investigate or dismiss.

questions.prompt: An investigator confirms that a flagged sign-in was in fact the legitimate user. What should they do in ID Protection to help improve detection?
questions.explanation: Admin feedback like confirming safe or compromised updates risk and helps improve the machine learning models.

questions.prompt: A company wants admins to hold privileged roles only when needed, with activation logged and time-limited. What is the main purpose of the Microsoft Entra feature it should use?
choices: To synchronize on-premises users and groups to the cloud
To provide just-in-time, monitored access to privileged roles
To block legacy authentication protocols across the tenant
To scan documents for sensitive information such as PII
questions.explanation: PIM reduces standing privileged access by making roles eligible and activating them just in time, with approval, justification and auditing.

questions.prompt: In PIM, what is the difference between an eligible and an active role assignment?
choices: Eligible roles must be activated before use; active roles need no activation
Eligible roles never expire, while active role assignments always expire
Active roles require approval each time, while eligible roles never do
Eligible roles apply only to guests, while active roles apply to members
questions.explanation: Eligible assignments require the user to perform an activation (possibly with MFA, justification or approval) before gaining the role's permissions.

questions.prompt: An admin needs Global Administrator rights only occasionally. To reduce risk, how should the role be assigned in PIM?
choices: Through membership in a dynamic membership group
By sharing the emergency access account password
As an eligible assignment activated for a limited time
As a permanent active assignment with no expiration
questions.explanation: Eligible, time-bound activation follows least privilege and limits the window in which the powerful role is exposed.

questions.prompt: Which PIM setting can require another person to approve before a privileged role becomes active?
questions.explanation: PIM role settings can require one or more approvers to approve activation requests.

questions.prompt: Which license is required for users who use Privileged Identity Management?
choices: Microsoft Entra ID P2 or ID Governance
Microsoft Entra ID P1 by itself
questions.explanation: PIM is a Microsoft Entra ID P2 (and Microsoft Entra ID Governance) capability.

questions.prompt: Besides Microsoft Entra roles, which other type of role can PIM manage just-in-time access for?
choices: SharePoint site theme and branding permissions
Local administrator rights on on-premises servers
Exchange mailbox folder permissions for delegates
Azure resource roles, such as Owner or Contributor
questions.explanation: PIM can manage Microsoft Entra roles, Azure resource roles, and membership or ownership of groups (PIM for Groups).

questions.prompt: During a PIM role activation, a user is asked to provide a business reason. Which setting causes this?
questions.explanation: Requiring justification records why the user activated the privileged role, supporting auditing.

questions.prompt: What is the PRIMARY benefit of PIM access reviews for privileged roles?
choices: Automatically creating new administrator accounts each quarter
Confirming that role holders still need their privileged access
Allowing guest users to assign privileged roles to themselves
Encrypting privileged role assignments when they are at rest
questions.explanation: Access reviews let reviewers attest whether role holders still need access, removing stale privileges.

questions.prompt: What is Microsoft Entra ID Governance?
choices: A tool for writing and linking Group Policy Objects to domains
Capabilities that ensure the right people have the right access at the right time
A data classification engine that labels documents and email
A firewall service that filters traffic to Azure virtual networks
questions.explanation: ID Governance covers the identity lifecycle, access lifecycle and privileged access, including entitlement management, access reviews, lifecycle workflows and PIM.

questions.prompt: What is the identity lifecycle often summarized as in Microsoft Entra ID Governance?
questions.explanation: Identity governance manages access as people join, change roles (move) and leave the organization.

questions.prompt: An auditor asks how the company regularly confirms that users still need their access. What are Microsoft Entra access reviews used for?
choices: Reviewing whether users still need group, app, or role access
Recording which mailboxes are placed on eDiscovery hold
Reviewing Azure spending and cost anomalies each month
Scanning application source code for vulnerabilities
questions.explanation: Access reviews let owners, managers or users themselves attest whether access is still needed, so stale access can be removed.

questions.prompt: A company wants managers to confirm every quarter that guest users still need access to a project Team. What should it configure?
choices: A Conditional Access named location policy
A recurring access review of guest members
Seamless single sign-on for the Team
questions.explanation: Recurring access reviews can target guests in Microsoft 365 groups or Teams and remove access that reviewers deny.

questions.prompt: In an access review, which option lets users confirm their own continued need for access?
choices: Reviewing by the Global Administrator only
questions.explanation: Access reviews can be performed by resource owners, managers, specific reviewers, or the users themselves.

questions.prompt: What can access reviews do automatically when a reviewer doesn't respond before the review ends?
choices: Delete the reviewer's account from the tenant
Extend the review indefinitely until someone responds
Assign the Global Administrator role to the user
Apply a default action, such as removing access
questions.explanation: Settings such as 'if reviewers don't respond' and auto-apply results let the review take action, including removing access or following system recommendations.

questions.prompt: A project lead wants a self-service way for people to request a bundle of resources. What does entitlement management in Microsoft Entra ID Governance provide?
choices: Scheduled antivirus scans for corporate endpoints and servers
Retention labels that keep email for a defined period
Conditional Access policies that block legacy authentication
Access packages with request, approval, and expiration workflows
questions.explanation: Entitlement management lets admins bundle groups, apps and SharePoint sites into access packages with policies for who can request and for how long.

questions.prompt: A project needs external partners to request access to a Team, a SharePoint site, and an app in one step, with access expiring after 90 days. What should the admin create?
choices: An access package in entitlement management
questions.explanation: Access packages bundle multiple resources and can allow external users to request access with approvals and automatic expiration.

questions.prompt: In entitlement management, what is a catalog?
choices: A collection of Conditional Access policies applied to a group
A list of risky sign-ins detected by Microsoft Entra ID Protection
A container of resources and access packages that can be delegated
A record of all eDiscovery cases opened in Microsoft Purview
questions.explanation: Catalogs group related resources and access packages, letting admins delegate management to non-administrators.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra ID Governance feature automates tasks such as sending a welcome email before a new hire's start date or removing access on their last day?
questions.explanation: Lifecycle workflows automate joiner, mover and leaver tasks based on user attributes such as employee hire date.

questions.prompt: What does 'terms of use' in Microsoft Entra ID allow an organization to do?
choices: Encrypt files with customer-managed keys stored in Key Vault
Disable guest invitations for users outside the IT department
Set password length and complexity requirements for all users
Require users to accept policies or disclaimers before accessing resources
questions.explanation: Terms of use policies present information users must accept, and Conditional Access can require acceptance before access.

questions.prompt: What is Microsoft Entra role-based access control (RBAC) used for?
choices: Monitoring network traffic between virtual networks
Granting admins only the permissions their tasks require
Scheduling operating system updates for managed devices
Classifying documents according to their sensitivity
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra roles, built-in or custom, grant only the permissions needed for administrative tasks.

questions.prompt: An admin only needs to reset passwords for non-admin users. Which approach BEST follows least privilege?
choices: Assign the Password Administrator or Helpdesk Administrator role
Assign the Privileged Role Administrator role to the admin
Make the admin an owner of every security group in the tenant
Assign the Global Administrator role permanently to the admin
questions.explanation: Narrow built-in roles grant password reset rights without the broad permissions of Global Administrator.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra role has access to all administrative features and should be assigned to as few people as possible?
questions.explanation: Global Administrator can manage all aspects of the tenant; Microsoft recommends fewer than five holders.

questions.prompt: A regional IT team should manage users only in the Europe division of the tenant. What should be used to scope their role?
questions.explanation: Administrative units restrict the scope of role permissions to a subset of users, groups or devices.

questions.prompt: When are custom roles in Microsoft Entra ID useful?
choices: When no built-in role matches the permissions needed
When a user needs to reset their own forgotten password
When guest users need to sign in to a shared Team
When a device must be marked compliant by Intune
questions.explanation: Custom roles let organizations combine specific permissions into a role definition when built-in roles are too broad or narrow.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Azure RBAC and Microsoft Entra roles is correct?
choices: Microsoft Entra roles manage the directory; Azure RBAC manages Azure resources
Azure RBAC manages users and groups in the Microsoft Entra directory
Microsoft Entra roles control access only to Azure virtual machines
They are the same set of roles managed from the same blade
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra roles control directory and identity tasks; Azure RBAC roles such as Owner, Contributor and Reader control Azure resource management.

questions.prompt: An admin is planning for a federation outage that could lock everyone out of the tenant. What is an emergency access (break-glass) account?
choices: A shared account that admins use for daily administrative work
A highly privileged cloud-only account reserved for emergencies
An account automatically created for each managed identity
A guest account given to external auditors during reviews
questions.explanation: Emergency access accounts prevent lockout of the tenant, for example if MFA or federation fails; they should be monitored closely.

questions.prompt: Which feature provides single sign-on for users on domain-joined devices on the corporate network, without them typing passwords to access cloud apps?
questions.explanation: Seamless SSO signs in users on corporate devices automatically when combined with password hash sync or pass-through authentication.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra ID capability lets users access on-premises web applications remotely through Microsoft Entra ID without opening inbound firewall ports?
questions.explanation: Application proxy uses an outbound connector to publish on-premises web apps securely through Microsoft Entra ID.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra feature shows a score and recommendations to help improve an organization's identity security posture?
questions.explanation: Identity Secure Score measures how well an organization follows Microsoft's identity security best practices and suggests improvements.

questions.prompt: A company wants to sign in employees to a third-party SaaS app such as Salesforce using their Microsoft Entra accounts. What should it configure?
choices: An enterprise application configured for SSO
A new AD DS forest dedicated to the SaaS app
A Microsoft Purview retention policy for the app
An eDiscovery hold on the users' mailboxes
questions.explanation: Adding the SaaS app as an enterprise application allows SSO using protocols like SAML or OpenID Connect.

questions.prompt: Which open standards does Microsoft Entra ID use for modern authentication and authorization with apps?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID is built around modern web protocols such as OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect and SAML.

questions.prompt: What does app registration in Microsoft Entra ID create?
choices: A guest user account for an external partner
A device record for a corporate-owned laptop
An application object for the app to use Microsoft Entra ID
A sensitivity label used to classify documents
questions.explanation: Registering an app creates an application object; a service principal is then created in each tenant where the app is used.

questions.prompt: A company is moving a legacy app that needs LDAP and Kerberos to Azure but doesn't want to run domain controllers. What does Microsoft Entra Domain Services provide?
choices: A managed service providing domain join, Group Policy, LDAP, and Kerberos
A synchronization tool that copies cloud users to on-premises AD DS
A DNS registrar used to purchase and renew public domain names
A certificate authority that issues public TLS certificates for websites
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Domain Services provides managed AD DS-compatible features so legacy apps can run in the cloud without managing DCs.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra licensing tier includes Microsoft Entra ID Protection and Privileged Identity Management?
questions.explanation: P2 adds ID Protection and PIM on top of P1 capabilities like Conditional Access.

questions.prompt: What are workload identities in Microsoft Entra ID?
choices: Shared mailbox accounts used by teams for customer email
Identities used by applications, services, and scripts
Guest users who work for vendors on short-term projects
Accounts created for employees who work in rotating shifts
questions.explanation: Workload identities include applications, service principals and managed identities used by software to authenticate.

questions.prompt: Which risk applies to service principals and can be detected by ID Protection for workload identities?
choices: Low mailbox storage for the app's owner account
Leaked or suspicious credentials for the app
Atypical travel by the app's original developer
Missing sensitivity labels on the app's documents
questions.explanation: ID Protection can detect risky workload identities, for example when app credentials are leaked, and Conditional Access can block them.

questions.prompt: Where can an admin view details of each user sign-in to Microsoft Entra ID, including status, location, and applied Conditional Access policies?
questions.explanation: Sign-in logs record each sign-in attempt and which Conditional Access policies applied and their results.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra logs record changes such as a user being added to a group or a role being assigned?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra audit logs capture directory changes like user, group, role and application updates.

questions.prompt: An admin wants Microsoft Entra ID to automatically create user accounts in a SaaS app like ServiceNow when users are assigned to it. Which feature should be used?
choices: Seamless single sign-on to the app
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra provisioning uses SCIM to create, update and remove accounts in connected apps automatically.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Microsoft Entra ID Free is correct?
choices: It requires at least one on-premises domain controller
It includes security defaults but not Conditional Access
It cannot be used by organizations that use Microsoft 365
It includes Privileged Identity Management and ID Protection
questions.explanation: The Free tier offers core identity features and security defaults; Conditional Access requires P1 and PIM/ID Protection require P2.

questions.prompt: A security team wants to require phishing-resistant MFA for administrators. Which Conditional Access feature lets them specify which MFA methods satisfy the policy?
questions.explanation: Authentication strengths let Conditional Access require specific method combinations, such as phishing-resistant MFA.

questions.prompt: How does number matching in Microsoft Authenticator help defend against MFA fatigue attacks?
choices: The app places a voice call to confirm each request
The app sends an SMS code to the user's backup phone
Users must enter the number shown on screen to approve
The app approves automatically after three prompts
questions.explanation: Number matching prevents users from blindly approving repeated push notifications sent by attackers.

questions.prompt: A user receives many unexpected MFA push prompts in a row late at night. What type of attack is MOST likely?
questions.explanation: Attackers with a valid password send repeated MFA prompts hoping the user approves one; number matching and phishing-resistant methods help mitigate this.

questions.prompt: Which Conditional Access assignment lets an admin target policies at specific apps, such as Office 365 or the Azure portal?
questions.explanation: Target resources specify which cloud apps or actions a policy applies to.

questions.prompt: What should an admin do to prevent Conditional Access policies from locking out all administrators?
choices: Assign every policy to all users with no exclusions
Exclude emergency access accounts from the policies
questions.explanation: Excluding monitored break-glass accounts from Conditional Access ensures access can be recovered if a policy is misconfigured.

questions.prompt: Which grant control can Conditional Access use to ensure users access email only through approved mobile apps such as Outlook?
choices: Require password change at the next sign-in
Block access from legacy authentication clients
Require acceptance of the terms of use policy
Require approved client app or app protection policy
questions.explanation: Conditional Access can require approved client apps or Intune app protection policies on mobile devices.

questions.prompt: Which session control in Conditional Access can route a session through Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps for real-time monitoring?
questions.explanation: Conditional Access App Control proxies sessions through Defender for Cloud Apps to monitor and control activities like downloads.

questions.prompt: A company has Microsoft Entra ID P1 and wants different Conditional Access rules for its Windows and iOS devices. Which signal condition should it use?
questions.explanation: The device platforms condition lets policies target specific operating systems such as Windows, iOS or Android.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra feature lets admins define trusted IP ranges or countries for use in Conditional Access?
questions.explanation: Named locations define IP ranges or countries/regions that Conditional Access policies can include or exclude.

questions.prompt: What happens when a user who is in scope of a Conditional Access policy requiring MFA has not registered any MFA methods?
choices: Access is granted without any MFA challenge
The policy is skipped automatically for the user
The user is prompted to register for MFA first
The user account is deleted from the tenant
questions.explanation: Users who must satisfy MFA but haven't registered are taken through registration so they can complete the requirement.

questions.prompt: Which external identity scenario lets users from another organization access your apps while still being managed by their home organization?
questions.explanation: With B2B, external users authenticate with their home identity provider; their account lifecycle stays with their organization.

questions.prompt: Which one-time passcode option lets a B2B guest without a Microsoft Entra or Microsoft account sign in?
questions.explanation: Email one-time passcode sends a code to the guest's email address so they can authenticate without an existing account.

questions.prompt: A company invites a partner whose users have Google accounts. Which capability allows those users to sign in as guests with Google?
questions.explanation: External ID supports federating with Google so guests can sign in with their Google accounts.

questions.prompt: A company wants users to be eligible for membership in a privileged security group and activate it only when needed. What does PIM for Groups allow?
choices: Creation of dynamic distribution lists in Exchange
Applying sensitivity labels to Microsoft Teams teams
Blocking guest invitations to all security groups
questions.explanation: PIM for Groups lets users be eligible for group membership or ownership and activate it only when needed.

questions.prompt: A company wants the access of contractors in an access package to end automatically on a set date. Which entitlement management setting supports this?
choices: An expiration setting on the access package policy
A custom banned password list for contractor accounts
A password writeback rule for contractor accounts
A Conditional Access named location for contractors
questions.explanation: Access package policies can set assignment expiration so access is removed automatically after a period or date.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra capability can periodically confirm whether guest users still need access and then block and delete the guests whose access is denied?
questions.explanation: Access reviews of guests can block sign-in for denied users and delete them after a period.

questions.prompt: What does the Conditional Access condition 'client apps' allow an admin to target?
choices: Documents that have a specific Microsoft Purview retention label
Azure subscriptions that have exceeded their monthly budgets
Users based on their job title and department attributes
Client types such as browsers, mobile and desktop apps, or legacy clients
questions.explanation: The client apps condition differentiates modern clients from legacy authentication clients, enabling policies such as blocking legacy auth.

questions.prompt: Where can a customer download Microsoft's independent audit reports, such as ISO 27001 and SOC reports, for Microsoft cloud services?
questions.explanation: The Service Trust Portal publishes audit reports, compliance guides and other trust documents about how Microsoft cloud services protect data.

questions.prompt: A compliance officer needs Microsoft's SOC 2 report for Microsoft 365 to share with an external auditor. What is the BEST place to obtain it?
choices: The Compliance Manager improvement actions page
questions.explanation: Audit reports for Microsoft cloud services are published on the Service Trust Portal for download.

questions.prompt: What must a user typically do to access and download most documents in the Service Trust Portal?
choices: Purchase a Microsoft Purview add-on license for the tenant
Register the organization as a Microsoft partner first
Sign in with a Microsoft cloud services account and accept the terms
Open a support ticket with Microsoft and wait for approval
questions.explanation: Many Service Trust Portal documents require signing in with a Microsoft cloud services account and agreeing to the terms and conditions.

questions.prompt: Which Service Trust Portal feature lets a user save documents for quick access later?
questions.explanation: My Library in the Service Trust Portal lets users save documents and receive notifications when they're updated.

questions.prompt: Which list contains only Microsoft privacy principles?
choices: Verify explicitly, least privilege, and assume breach
questions.explanation: Microsoft's six privacy principles are control, transparency, security, strong legal protections, no content-based targeting, and benefits to you. The other lists are Zero Trust principles, the CIA triad and GRC.

questions.prompt: Under Microsoft's privacy principle of 'no content-based targeting', what does Microsoft commit to?
choices: Not storing any customer data outside the United States
Not responding to any government requests for customer data
Not using personal content like email or files to target ads
Not encrypting customer data at rest in its datacenters
questions.explanation: Microsoft commits not to use customers' personal content to target ads.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft privacy principle states that Microsoft puts customers in control of their privacy with easy-to-use tools and clear choices?
questions.explanation: The control principle means customers decide how their data is collected and used, with tools and clear choices.

questions.prompt: Microsoft explains how it collects and uses data so customers can make informed decisions. Which privacy principle is this?
questions.explanation: Transparency means being open about data collection and use.

questions.prompt: Microsoft commits to respecting local privacy laws and defending the fundamental right to privacy. Which privacy principle does this describe?
questions.explanation: Strong legal protections covers respecting privacy laws and fighting for legal protection of privacy as a fundamental right.

questions.prompt: When Microsoft collects data, it uses it to benefit customers and make their experiences better. Which privacy principle is this?
questions.explanation: The benefits to you principle says data Microsoft collects is used to improve the customer's experience.

questions.prompt: Microsoft protects the data customers entrust to it through strong security and encryption. Which privacy principle is this?
questions.explanation: The security principle commits Microsoft to protecting customer data with strong security and encryption.

questions.prompt: A new compliance officer asks what Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager is for. What is the BEST description?
choices: A tool that tracks compliance requirements and measures progress with a score
A service that places legal holds on mailboxes during litigation
A policy engine that requires MFA based on sign-in conditions
A portal that stores Microsoft's ISO and SOC audit reports for download
questions.explanation: Compliance Manager provides assessments, improvement actions and a compliance score to help organizations manage regulatory requirements.

questions.prompt: A company must demonstrate progress toward GDPR requirements across its Microsoft 365 environment. Which Microsoft Purview tool BEST supports this?
choices: Compliance Manager with a GDPR assessment
questions.explanation: Compliance Manager assessments map controls and improvement actions to regulations like GDPR and track progress through the compliance score.

questions.prompt: A CIO asks what the compliance score on the Compliance Manager dashboard represents. What does it measure?
choices: The number of eDiscovery cases that are closed
The percentage of users who have MFA enabled
The percentage of email that is sent encrypted
Progress in completing recommended improvement actions
questions.explanation: The compliance score reflects points earned for completed improvement actions, helping organizations understand their compliance posture.

questions.prompt: In Compliance Manager, what is an assessment?
choices: A grouping of controls from a regulation or standard
A single entry recorded in the unified audit log
A legal hold placed on a custodian's mailbox
A document downloaded from the Service Trust Portal
questions.explanation: Assessments are built from templates and group the controls needed to meet a regulation or standard.

questions.prompt: In Compliance Manager, what is used as the basis for creating an assessment?
questions.explanation: Templates contain the controls and actions for a regulation or standard; assessments are created from them.

questions.prompt: Which Compliance Manager element provides guidance on how to implement controls to help meet regulatory requirements?
questions.explanation: Improvement actions give step-by-step guidance and centralize evidence and implementation details for controls.

questions.prompt: Which type of control in Compliance Manager is implemented by Microsoft and requires no action from the customer?
questions.explanation: Microsoft-managed controls cover Microsoft's responsibilities for its cloud services; customers don't need to act on them.

questions.prompt: A Compliance Manager control requires both Microsoft and the customer to take action. What type of control is this?
questions.explanation: Shared controls are the joint responsibility of Microsoft and the customer.

questions.prompt: What are 'your controls' in Compliance Manager?
choices: Controls that Microsoft implements for the customer
Controls the customer is solely responsible for implementing
Controls that apply only to on-premises AD DS
questions.explanation: Your controls, also called customer-managed controls, are implemented and managed entirely by the organization.

questions.prompt: What is the default assessment that Compliance Manager provides to give an initial compliance score?
questions.explanation: Compliance Manager provides a data protection baseline assessment for Microsoft 365 by default, which produces the initial score.

questions.prompt: In Compliance Manager scoring, which kind of action typically earns MORE points: a mandatory preventative action or a discretionary detective action?
choices: Neither earns points toward the score
They always earn the same points
questions.explanation: Actions are weighted by type and whether they are mandatory or discretionary; mandatory and preventative actions carry higher point values.

questions.prompt: Which Compliance Manager action type is designed to identify and alert on irregular activity, such as reviewing audit logs?
questions.explanation: Detective actions monitor systems to identify irregular activity, while preventative actions block risks and corrective actions limit damage after an incident.

questions.prompt: An improvement action to encrypt data at rest so it cannot be read if stolen is an example of which action type?
questions.explanation: Preventative actions address specific risks before they occur, such as encrypting data or blocking unauthorized access.

questions.prompt: A legal team is preparing for a lawsuit. What is the PRIMARY purpose of eDiscovery in Microsoft Purview?
choices: To find, preserve, and deliver content as evidence for legal cases
To find misconfigured Conditional Access policies in a tenant
To scan source code repositories for exposed secrets and keys
To discover unmanaged devices connected to the corporate network
questions.explanation: eDiscovery identifies and delivers electronic content such as email and documents for legal investigations and litigation.

questions.prompt: During litigation, a company must ensure that a former manager's mailbox and OneDrive content cannot be deleted. What should it do in eDiscovery?
choices: Place the content locations on hold
Assign the user an eligible PIM role
questions.explanation: eDiscovery holds preserve content in specified locations so it cannot be permanently deleted while the case is active.

questions.prompt: A legal team adds a sales director to an eDiscovery (Premium) case as a custodian. What is a custodian?
choices: A Microsoft employee who reviews customer data
A person who controls data relevant to a case
An auditor who downloads Service Trust Portal reports
A user who approves PIM role activation requests
questions.explanation: Custodians are people whose data is relevant to a case; eDiscovery (Premium) can manage custodians, place holds and send legal hold notifications.

questions.prompt: Which eDiscovery (Premium) capability lets legal teams analyze, tag, and review collected content within the case?
questions.explanation: Review sets hold a static copy of collected content so teams can analyze, query, tag and annotate it.

questions.prompt: Which eDiscovery (Premium) feature notifies custodians that they must preserve content related to a case?
questions.explanation: eDiscovery (Premium) can send and track legal hold notifications to custodians.

questions.prompt: Which feature of eDiscovery (Premium) groups near-duplicate documents and email threads to reduce review volume?
choices: Near-duplicate detection and email threading analytics
Compliance score weighting of improvement actions
Audit log retention policies for Exchange records
Password hash synchronization with on-premises AD DS
questions.explanation: eDiscovery (Premium) analytics reduce the amount of content to review by identifying near-duplicates and threading email.

questions.prompt: Which role group gives a user permission to create and manage eDiscovery cases they are a member of?
questions.explanation: Members of the eDiscovery Manager role group can create and manage cases; eDiscovery Administrators can access all cases.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between an eDiscovery Manager and an eDiscovery Administrator?
choices: The two role groups have identical permissions and differ only in their names
An eDiscovery Manager can manage all cases; an Administrator only their own cases
An eDiscovery Administrator can manage all cases; a Manager only cases they belong to
Only eDiscovery Managers can export data; Administrators can only view cases
questions.explanation: eDiscovery Administrators are members of the eDiscovery Manager role group with extra rights to view and manage all cases in the organization.

questions.prompt: A security analyst is asked to investigate suspicious activity in Microsoft 365. What is Microsoft Purview Audit used for?
choices: Scoring an organization's progress against regulations like GDPR
Requiring MFA when Microsoft Entra ID detects a risky sign-in
Recording user and admin activity so it can be searched and investigated
Downloading Microsoft's independent SOC and ISO audit reports
questions.explanation: Audit captures activities such as file access, mailbox actions and admin changes into a searchable unified audit log.

questions.prompt: A security investigator needs to find out who deleted a SharePoint document last week. Which Microsoft Purview solution should they use?
questions.explanation: Searching the unified audit log shows who performed activities such as deleting files, and when.

questions.prompt: How long are audit records retained by default with Microsoft Purview Audit (Standard)?
questions.explanation: Audit (Standard) retains records for 180 days by default. Longer retention requires Audit (Premium).

questions.prompt: What is the default retention period for Exchange, SharePoint, and Microsoft Entra audit records with Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium)?
questions.explanation: Audit (Premium) keeps those audit records for one year by default, and custom retention policies can retain records up to 10 years with an add-on license.

questions.prompt: An organization must keep audit records for up to 10 years to meet regulatory requirements. Which solution supports this?
choices: Audit (Standard) with its default retention settings
Microsoft Entra sign-in logs exported monthly
Documents saved to the Service Trust Portal
questions.explanation: Audit (Premium) supports audit log retention policies, and 10-year retention requires an add-on license.

questions.prompt: Which capability of Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium) helps investigators determine whether email was accessed during a compromise?
choices: My Library in the Service Trust Portal
Review sets in an eDiscovery case
questions.explanation: Audit (Premium) logs crucial events like MailItemsAccessed and Send, helping investigators scope a breach.

questions.prompt: Besides longer retention and crucial events, which other benefit does Microsoft Purview Audit (Premium) provide?
choices: Free downloads of Microsoft's own audit reports
Automatic legal holds on every user mailbox
Higher-bandwidth access to the Office 365 Management Activity API
Built-in compliance score templates for audits
questions.explanation: Audit (Premium) gives organizations higher bandwidth to the Management Activity API for faster access to audit data.

questions.prompt: What must be true for user and admin activity to be recorded in the audit log?
choices: An eDiscovery case must be open for the user
Each user must enable auditing individually
Every user must have a Microsoft Entra ID P2 license
Auditing must be turned on for the organization
questions.explanation: Audit log recording must be enabled for the organization; it is on by default for most Microsoft 365 organizations.

questions.prompt: Which Azure service is designed specifically to mitigate volumetric and protocol attacks that attempt to overwhelm Azure resources with traffic?
questions.explanation: Azure DDoS Protection monitors traffic and mitigates distributed denial-of-service attacks at network layers 3 and 4.

questions.prompt: A company wants DDoS mitigation for only two public IP addresses rather than an entire virtual network. Which Azure DDoS Protection tier BEST fits?
questions.explanation: DDoS IP Protection is billed per protected public IP, while DDoS Network Protection covers all public IPs in the virtual networks it is enabled on.

questions.prompt: Which feature is included with Azure DDoS Network Protection but NOT with DDoS IP Protection?
choices: Always-on traffic monitoring of the IP
Access to the DDoS Rapid Response team
Attack mitigation reports and flow logs
questions.explanation: DDoS Rapid Response support, cost protection and WAF discounts come with Network Protection; core monitoring, tuning and reports exist in both tiers.

questions.prompt: An attacker floods a web app with valid-looking HTTP requests at layer 7. Which service should be added alongside Azure DDoS Protection to address this?
questions.explanation: Azure DDoS Protection focuses on layers 3 and 4; application-layer (layer 7) attacks are best handled with a WAF, for example on Application Gateway or Front Door.

questions.prompt: Which type of DDoS attack attempts to exhaust server resources by exploiting weaknesses in layer 3 and layer 4 protocols, such as a SYN flood?
